record.paper_title: Open problems on structure of positively curved projective varieties
record.original_question: Let X be a projective variety with mild singularities, for example klt singularities. An MRC fibration is a rational map φ: X ⇢ Y whose general fibers are compact and rationally connected and such that no horizontal rational curve passes through a very general point of X; the birational model of the base Y is not uniquely determined. Under what conditions can one choose the birational model Y so that the MRC fibration is represented by a holomorphic map rather than only an almost holomorphic rational map?

evidence.quote: A rational map φ : X ⇢ Y is called an RC fibration (resp. MRC fibration) if it satisfies the first two conditions (resp. all the conditions) below:
General fibers of φ : X ⇢ Y are rationally connected.
There is no horizontal rational curve (i.e., no rational curve whose image under φ is not one point) passing through a very general point in X.
Problem 2.1. — When do we choose an MRC fibration to be holomorphic from the ambiguities in the choices of Y ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a normal projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$ with mild singularities (for example, Kawamata log terminal singularities). A maximal rationally connected (MRC) fibration of $X$ is a dominant rational map $\varphi: X \dashrightarrow Y$ to a normal projective variety $Y$ such that:

(i) the general fiber of $\varphi$ is compact and rationally connected, and

(ii) no horizontal rational curve (i.e., a rational curve in $X$ whose image under $\varphi$ is not a single point) passes through a very general point of $X$.

Such an MRC fibration always exists, but the birational model of the base $Y$ is not uniquely determined: any birationally equivalent model $Y'$ produces another MRC fibration $X \dashrightarrow Y'$.

Determine sufficient conditions on $X$ (and a procedure for choosing the birational model $Y$) under which one can ensure that the MRC fibration $\varphi: X \dashrightarrow Y$ is represented by a holomorphic morphism $X \to Y$ rather than only an almost holomorphic rational map.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work establishes the existence of a model of the MRC fibration that is a projective morphism for normal compact Kähler spaces with klt singularities, and structure theorems for projective klt pairs with nef anti-canonical divisor show that after a finite quasi-étale cover one obtains a holomorphic MRC fibration onto a klt base. These results provide significant progress but the general question of when a holomorphic MRC model can be chosen remains an active area, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Structure theorem for projective klt pairs with nef anti-canonical divisor
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a finite quasi-étale cover X′ → X where X′ admits a holomorphic MRC fibration ψ: X′ → Y, where Y is a projective klt variety with numerically trivial canonical divisor.
status_evidence.claim: After a finite quasi-étale cover, a holomorphic MRC fibration exists onto a klt base with numerically trivial canonical divisor.

status_evidence.title: Projectivity criteria for Kähler morphisms
status_evidence.snippet: There exists a model of the MRC fibration that is a projective morphism for normal compact Kähler spaces with klt singularities.
status_evidence.claim: A projective-morphism model of the MRC fibration exists in the klt Kähler setting.
